title: Machado Signals Openness to Election Negotiations with Venezuela's Transitional Government
detail: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado signaled on May 29, 2026 that she is willing to enter formal negotiations with Acting President Delcy Rodríguez's transitional government over a pathway to competitive presidential elections, according to Bloomberg and regional media. Machado's Democratic Unitary Platform is seeking 'a serious, firm, and responsible negotiation' with the interim government to establish conditions for a credible election, which the opposition estimates requires 7–9 months of preparation. Key conditions include: appointment of genuinely independent CNE electoral authorities; restoration of eligibility for all previously banned candidates; updated voter registration rolls; comprehensive international observation; and a committed timeline for orderly transfer of power. Machado, who announced her presidential candidacy from Panama City on May 23 and won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize for her sustained democracy advocacy, plans to return to Venezuela from exile before the end of 2026. The announcement follows the Trump administration's deepening engagement with Rodríguez's government — including the controversial May 27 directive not to pursue criminal probes against Rodríguez — suggesting a broader US-brokered framework for Venezuela's political normalization is taking shape. Norwegian mediators who facilitated the 2023 Barbados Agreement are reportedly involved in preliminary contacts between the opposition and the transitional government.

media.caption: María Corina Machado signals readiness to negotiate with Venezuela's interim government on competitive election timeline
